A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Jacobian and hidden-trajectory study, despite the changed title and expanded scope. Their main text, equations, figures, model table, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements of Jacobian alignment, trajectory linearity, exponential growth, and singular-value scaling in trained and randomly initialized LLMs (Section 4 and Appendix A.4).

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical measurements and adds cross-token coupling, training-checkpoint analyses, and supplementary representation and sensitivity results (Section 5 and Appendix A.6).

M1.justification: v1 analyzes a token's self-Jacobian across layers. v2 Section 3.1 generalizes this to input-output token-pair Jacobians and introduces coupling analyses with matching input/output tokens, fixed input tokens, and fixed output tokens. This substantially extends the analytical procedure beyond renaming alignment.

E1.justification: The six leaderboard datasets are retained. v2 Figure 19 additionally uses WikiText-2 prompts for representation and logit-entropy measurements, adding general-text input coverage within the existing language-model analysis.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 25 adds explicit comparisons of coupling with parameter count, layer count, and embedding dimension as predictors of benchmark performance. These competing reference predictors were not evaluated in the corresponding correlation analysis in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds Pythia checkpoint evaluations, normalized coupling with a layer-separation restriction, 11-layer measurement windows, and K=25/50/75/100 sensitivity settings. Expodistance also changes from growth rates of layer increments relative to the initial increment to adjacent representation-norm ratios (v1 Section 3.4 versus v2 Section 3.3). The original growth plot is nevertheless reused, so the PDFs do not establish that its measurements were recomputed under the revised definition.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of training-time emergence, sensitivity to the number of singular vectors, associations with model properties and positional encoding, and depth-resolved norms, linearity, spacing, and logit entropy (Figures 2, 4, 19–22, 25–29). These substantially expand the questions examined beyond v1's endpoint comparisons and spectral analyses.

E5.justification: The existing median and interquartile-range reporting is retained. New checkpoint plots, including Figures 4 and 21, display mean curves with extrema or range information. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts or significance tests; the added bands describe variability rather than establishing uncertainty across independent training runs.

E6.justification: The headline R²=0.7214 and reported mean LSS values of 4.25 trained versus 6.54 untrained remain. v2 adds cross-token and checkpoint results; Figure 25 reports benchmark R² values of 0.3254, 0.3547, and 0.3614 for depth, embedding dimension, and parameter count. Figure 26 adds R² values from 0.7331 at K=25 to 0.6933 at K=100. v1 Figure 3's fine-tuned-inclusive correlation panel is omitted.

T1.justification: v2 extends the mathematical definitions to token-pair coupling, introduces normalized mis-coupling, and revises the exponential-rate definition. Section 7 adds a short gradient-update argument linking coupling to in-context learning. The SVD framework and appendix linear-ODE derivation remain substantially unchanged, with no new theorem or substantial proof development.

C1.justification: The contribution expands from depth-wise Transformer Alignment and trajectory regularity to coupling across both tokens and depth. The abstract and contributions also newly claim that coupling correlates more strongly with benchmark performance than parameter budget, model depth, or embedding dimension. These are substantive extensions of the central claims.

C2.justification: The in-context-learning discussion changes from claiming that coupling could only emerge through joint problem-solving to presenting a gradient-update analogy. v2 makes the exponential-growth explanation more explicitly conditional and adds layer normalization as a possible explanation for untrained singular-value scaling. The limitation concerning uncontrolled differences between independently trained models is retained.

D1.justification: Table 1 adds positional-encoding information and additional Pythia specifications, and corrects the Neo 2.7B and Pythia 6.9B parameter-unit entries. New captions disclose checkpoint selections, layer windows, and prompt counts. GPU, batching, quantization, and claimed supplementary-code information are retained; the smaller Jacobian prompt subset remains unspecified.

R1.justification: The existing dynamical-systems and Residual Alignment foundations remain. v2 sharpens the distinction through transformer-specific token interactions and adds references to Su et al., Sarfati et al., and Wu and Papyan, while removing the introductory Brown et al. and Devlin et al. references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten around transformer block coupling and explicit research questions. Evaluation is separated from Methods, while PCA methodology and the ResNet comparison move into the appendices. The changes substantially reorganize the presentation beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds a coupling schematic, token-interaction heatmaps, checkpoint curves, and numerous diagnostic panels. The correlation display changes from two panels to one and moves forward; LSS is reordered and duplicated in the appendix. Existing spectral figures are enlarged and rearranged, and Table 1 gains a positional-encoding column.

improvement.justification: v1 supports training emergence mainly through randomly initialized versus final-model comparisons. v2 directly examines Pythia checkpoints, tests singular-vector-count sensitivity, and establishes a distinct cross-token extension through several interaction cases. These substantially strengthen the empirical foundation and contribution. The unreconciled expodistance definition and reused plot, together with removal of the fine-tuned-inclusive correlation panel, weaken reporting but do not outweigh these gains.
